batch_strategy: Test the loading scope of the latest m124, m209 and m33 failures; distinguish genuine strong-solvent response features from corrections transferred across related graphs; and complete selected solvent-response and loading comparisons with measured anchors. Use predictions to identify discriminating comparisons, with CW distance as secondary coverage evidence.

choices.reason: m124 in pure EA at 106.4 mg tests whether the late, nearly coincident 18.51/18.55 mL endpoints measured at 53.2 mg in 0e09f8144b025e4b5a8a extend to the loading midpoint. The current late-onset prediction has already transferred across loading without a corresponding label.

m124 in pure EA at 159.6 mg completes the three-loading boundary comparison. Together with selected midpoint pure EA and 0e09f8144b025e4b5a8a, it distinguishes a broadly reproducible boundary response from a loading-specific or variable record; upper-loading 5/1 record df118a80070e524b9ecd3 supplies additional context.

m209 at 2/1 and 206.25 mg tests transfer of the exceptional midpoint result in 4fce6e1a422b4f54c601, measured 21.85/21.90 mL. The upper-loading prediction is also late and compact, although measured upper-loading 5/1 in edfbbb86c05a0aeb1bfb was 7.45/17.05 mL.

m209 at 1/1 and 137.5 mg fills the immediate stronger-solvent neighbor of exceptional 2/1 record 4fce6e1a422b4f54c601. It tests whether the late onset emerges abruptly after an ordinary 1/1 response, using same-loading 5/1 record a7ed4a556d5cae1eb7e1 as the other measured neighbor.

m209 in pure EA at 137.5 mg completes the selected pure-EA–1/1 segment before measured 2/1. Its predicted completion exceeds the selected 1/1 prediction, so the two labels can distinguish an early completion feature from an isolated 2/1 endpoint anomaly.

m33 at 50/1 and 99.7 mg tests the missing loading midpoint between completion 26.73 mL in 570497bf792f134f2223 and 39.01 mL in c356230277dfc98406e0. This discriminates a systematic completion-loading relationship from an exceptional upper-loading result while separately testing the low onset.

m33 at 20/1 and 99.7 mg pairs with selected midpoint 50/1. Lower- and upper-loading 20/1 records d13724f7a4b6c8bb3628 and 75328dcee739068fdfba finished near 23 mL; the pair determines whether onset decline and loading-dependent completion growth also occur at the midpoint.

Naphthalene m215 in pure EA at 50 mg predicts a late onset of 14.16 mL, followed by much earlier predicted onset at selected 1/1. This tests whether the new m124 pure-EA correction transfers to a fused aromatic graph without an ether; that transfer remains a model hypothesis.

m215 at 1/1 and 50 mg supplies the matched control for selected pure EA. Existing 5/1 and 20/1 observations 36767e257ec2c6a901ce and 9fc58dd991e905ad49bb provide context, but cannot establish the predicted strong-boundary decline at this loading.

Bromonaphthalene m7 in pure EA at 100 mg predicts onset 8.55 mL versus 4.72 mL at selected 1/1. This provides a second fused aromatic test of the strong-boundary feature after the unexpected m124 label, with measured 10/1 record 60ef3e08e4fa789b999c as a same-loading reference.

m7 at 1/1 and 100 mg completes the matched pure-EA comparison. It distinguishes a real onset decrease from a prediction transferred across fused aromatic structures, without assuming that the different recorded DCM volumes across molecules isolate a structural effect.

Long-chain dibromothiophene m71 in pure EA at 132.1 mg predicts completion 20.36 mL, well above selected 2/1 at 8.73 mL. Its sparse measured anchors a6fd9cae6e0672265c13 and 7e981ba02c83f74f5e65 motivate testing this large strong-region feature on a highly hydrophobic sulfur-containing graph.

m71 at 2/1 and 132.1 mg supplies the protocol-matched comparator for selected pure EA. The pair tests whether the predicted large decline is reproducible and helps constrain strong-condition transfer beyond the fused aromatic compounds.

Chloroketone m27 at 1/1 and 105.7 mg predicts completion 12.26 mL, whereas measured same-loading 10/1 and 20/1 records c0adb1c6f9dbe862a4dc and a3c1a0ac40733e8650fb finished near 6 mL. This tests an uncovered early maximum in a family with recorded loading-associated differences.

m27 at 2/1 and 105.7 mg connects selected 1/1 to the measured short middle-loading weak-condition responses. Lower-loading 2/1 and 10/1 records 504e8e25f3a8b339a023 and 09096996d08f0c063345 were longer, so this label helps distinguish solvent curvature from loading-specific behavior.

Alkylbenzene m132 at 1/1 and 86 mg anchors the stronger side of a predicted 2/1 completion maximum. Measured same-loading 5/1 and 10/1 records fdaa37b02fe0d59d96e9 and d0e8fd2b1d04ee0fd352 both finished near 6.5 mL, making this a locally testable hydrocarbon response curve.

m132 at 2/1 and 86 mg predicts completion 10.13 mL, above selected 1/1 and the measured 5/1 response in fdaa37b02fe0d59d96e9. The pair tests a remaining local maximum after the latest stilbene comparison removed a different predicted maximum.

Methoxybenzoate m87 in pure EA at 110.3 mg predicts a later onset than selected 1/1 despite stronger eluent. With measured 2/1 record 981a11d7d65c8e5597f9, the pair tests endpoint-specific strong-boundary curvature on an ester/ether graph.

m87 at 1/1 and 110.3 mg completes the matched pure-EA comparison and connects to measured 2/1 endpoints 4.74/13.51 mL in 981a11d7d65c8e5597f9. It determines whether the predicted onset minimum survives while completion increases.

Acetal-containing aryl ketone m39 in pure EA at 100 mg fills the boundary before measured 1/1 completion 15.88 mL in 162ffd9b0db1fd3c1509. Its high CW distance and relatively broad completion quantile span support checking this underanchored segment, without treating that span as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

Cyclic acetal ether m6 at 10/1 and 83.45 mg tests a predicted completion plateau or small maximum before selected 20/1. Measured same-loading 2/1 and 50/1 records 8398d446af24cfce2962 and b94677e12c4d6aa11d9b finished at 9.84 and 14.73 mL, providing a direct boundary to transfer from m116's much larger weak-solvent rise.

m6 at 20/1 and 83.45 mg completes the matched 10/1–20/1–50/1 segment around b94677e12c4d6aa11d9b. It distinguishes a genuine weak-region plateau from misplaced curvature and constrains the limits of an ether-wide retention correction.

Bromoanisole m113 at 50/1 and 224.1 mg extends measured same-loading 10/1 record 9d5283cf29e9f80d1912, which finished at 14.43 mL. The modest predicted growth to 16.62 mL tests whether weak-solvent flattening remains appropriate for a monomethoxy graph after m116's correction.

Chloroanisole m121 at 20/1 and 174.6 mg establishes an intermediate weak-condition anchor after measured 5/1 record db9851c0898e1d345de2. Paired with selected 50/1, it tests a sparsely measured halogenated ether curve instead of assuming that m116's response transfers.

m121 at 50/1 and 174.6 mg completes the selected weak segment from the measured 5/1 anchor db9851c0898e1d345de2. Its predicted completion is only 14.24 mL; measuring both 20/1 and 50/1 distinguishes sustained shallow growth from an uncovered later rise.

m39 at 5/1 and 50 mg supplies the lower-loading anchor for selected 20/1. Upper-loading 5/1 and 20/1 records ae8805bc02bce03072e2 and a6a0404c3ad65c6d9326 showed substantial growth, but do not establish its loading scope.

m39 at 20/1 and 50 mg completes a lower-loading solvent segment and directly compares with upper-loading a6a0404c3ad65c6d9326. This tests whether the model's nearly loading-insensitive completion prediction generalizes on a graph combining an acetal ring and ketone.

The latter acquisition overpredicted both endpoints, so this intermediate label can constrain curvature without applying a common offset to the entire curve.

Secondary alcohol m60 at 10/1 and 97 mg fills the loading midpoint between beda2205eedbe1688e1f and 5e45395722fa0dcc1d00. Their onsets decrease from 46.02 to 36.93 mL while completions remain near 66–69 mL, offering a useful endpoint-specific loading comparison against selected m51.

Upper-loading 5/1 record b51b5dbcd2a38b174973 measured 27.48/65.41 mL; this label tests transfer of that correction across loading on a basic heteroaromatic graph.

hypotheses.content: m120 has a strongly nonparallel and nonmonotonic recorded loading response. At 5/1, lower loading gives late onset and completion, the midpoint is much shorter, and upper loading has early onset but late completion. The previous completion-only interpretation is insufficient for the lower-loading boundary. Loading interactions, variability and associations with missing factors remain competing explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A single loading trend or common shift of both endpoints cannot represent these observations. This remains a warning against transferring a completion correction indiscriminately across loading or alcohol environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can additional matched solvent segments or independent catalog replicates reproduce the lower/midpoint/upper ordering? The supplied eligible rows do not provide the next directly discriminating m120 weak-solvent segment.

hypotheses.content: m116's substantial weak-solvent completion growth is now observed at all three loading levels, while onset retains a loading ordering. This strengthens transfer within m116 but still does not justify a uniform ether correction: measured dimethoxy, trimethoxy and cyclic-acetal examples have different response scales. The remaining shallow predictions for halogenated monoethers and the cyclic acetal require direct condition-response tests.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected curves can teach which ether environments support sustained growth and which plateau, limiting inappropriate transfer from a recently corrected scaffold.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do matched m6 10/1–20/1–50/1 labels support a plateau, and do m113 and m121 retain their predicted shallow weak-solvent growth?

hypotheses.content: Predicted extrema are useful local acquisition signals but are not findings or violations to remove automatically. Recent m10, m189 and m176 measurements removed particular predicted completion maxima or declines, while m155 retained a substantial strong-region decline and m171 retained a smaller decrease. Remaining features should be tested with matched neighboring conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched comparisons can repair solvent-response representations while preserving real endpoint-specific exceptions. Testing several relevant graph environments helps identify the boundaries of transfer.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which remaining strong-region features on m71, m27, m132, m87 and m39 survive matched measurements, and do onset and completion change together?

hypotheses.content: m33's 20/1-to-50/1 onset decline with completion growth is now observed at both loading extremes. Completion growth is much larger at upper loading: approximately 23.00 to 39.01 mL versus 23.22 to 26.73 mL at lower loading. The midpoint is needed to distinguish a systematic loading relationship from an exceptional upper-loading response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The relationship concerns separate endpoint responses and loading-dependent completion growth. A center-only correction or nearly loading-insensitive response could miss it.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does midpoint m33 preserve the onset decline, and does its 50/1 completion fall between the two measured loading extremes while 20/1 completion remains near 23 mL?

hypotheses.content: The late, nearly coincident pure-EA endpoints measured for lower-loading m124 may represent a reproducible boundary response, a loading-specific result or variability associated with missing factors. The current model has propagated late pure-EA onset to other m124 loadings and related fused aromatic graphs before those labels are available.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A large newly acquired onset correction could improve local prediction or spread an isolated response across many rows. Testing loading scope and related graphs can discriminate these outcomes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does late pure-EA onset persist at both other m124 loadings, and do protocol-matched pure-EA–1/1 comparisons on m215 and m7 support a related feature? Cross-molecule differences in loading protocol prevent a causal structural interpretation.

hypotheses.content: m209's midpoint 2/1 result, 21.85/21.90 mL, does not yet establish a transferable compact elution interval. Its earlier strong-condition curve and loading scope remain unresolved, and ordinary responses at neighboring ratios coexist with this exceptional record.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest failure affected both endpoints. Determining whether it is isolated or part of a sharp condition/loading response can prevent an unjustified shared correction across phenol/ether rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is upper-loading 2/1 similarly late and compact, and do midpoint pure EA and 1/1 show an ordinary baseline or an earlier feature leading into the exceptional 2/1 result?

feedback_interpretation: The largest change is that m120's lower-loading labels invalidate a completion-only account of its failure: 4ee22742c686bdbb1cb9 measured 19.89/29.02 mL at 2/1, and 71abc36775b6cce56da7 measured 50.73/71.53 mL at 5/1. Both endpoints were substantially underestimated at acquisition. Its loading response remains unresolved rather than supporting a simple overload rule. Available directly discriminating m120 follow-ups are limited, so this batch uses other matched loading comparisons without claiming they establish the m120 mechanism. For m116, completion near 53–56 mL at all three 50/1 loadings supports the corrected weak rise; lower-loading onset was still underestimated by 6.12 mL, while upper-loading 20/1 and 50/1 predictions were close. I therefore reduce further m116 sampling and test the structural boundaries of transfer. m33's upper-loading 50/1 completion was underestimated by 12.77 mL, despite a much smaller onset discrepancy, making its missing loading midpoint valuable. m67 now supports decreasing 20/1 onset across loading with comparatively similar completions, reinforcing endpoint-specific loading comparisons on m51 and m60. Most latest strong-region extrema did not survive: m10, m40 and m189 lost their proposed completion declines, m176 completion increased through 5/1–10/1–20/1, and m17 did not show the predicted interval collapse. However, m124 pure EA and m209 2/1 produced new late, nearly coincident endpoint records. These warrant tests of reproducibility and scope, not automatic propagation or dismissal. m55 and m63 gave mostly modest errors, reducing the immediate value of further dense interpolation on those curves. All stated prediction errors are acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The batch combines targeted failure repair with connected experiments that can identify where a learned correction should generalize. Seven labels investigate the loading or neighboring-condition scope of the new m124, m209 and m33 discrepancies. Matched strong-boundary comparisons on related fused aromatic graphs test whether the m124 correction is transferable, while additional hydrocarbon, sulfur, chloroketone and ester/ether comparisons examine remaining response features with direct controls. The m6, m113 and m121 weak-condition measurements place boundaries around transfer from the now-supported m116 rise. The remaining carbonyl, alcohol and pyridyl-ester experiments complete useful solvent transitions or loading comparisons, including cases where onset and completion may have different loading sensitivities. Multiple selections on one molecule form matched discrimination experiments; identical-condition candidate copies are not selected together. The expected benefit is a better structure–condition mapping for both endpoints across the Row-distribution, including common short responses and less well represented transitions. Chemical adsorption and solvent-strength expectations are priors, and exceptional labels may also reflect variability or absent experimental factors. Loading amount is density times sample volume; recorded loading solvent and its volume remain part of every comparison. Quantile spans are single-predictor summaries, CW distance is coverage evidence, and V2 minus V1 is the elution interval width. These 32 IDs and their exact associated premeasurement predictions in this packet are frozen together before any new label reveal.
